values.en: On $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$, let $X(u,v)=(u,v,0)$. Then $X_u=(1,0,0)$, $X_v=(0,1,0)$ and the ordered-cross-product unit normal is $\boldsymbol N=(0,0,1)$. Thus $E=G=1$, $F=0$, all second partials vanish, and $e=f=g=0$. At every $q$, for $w=aX_u+bX_v$ and $z=cX_u+dX_v$, $\mathrm I_X(q;w,z)=ac+bd$ and $\mathrm{II}_{X,\boldsymbol N}(q;w,z)=0$. The opposite normal still gives the zero second form.
values.zh-CN: 在 $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$ 上取 $X(u,v)=(u,v,0)$。则 $X_u=(1,0,0)$、$X_v=(0,1,0)$，有序叉积单位法向为 $\boldsymbol N=(0,0,1)$。因此 $E=G=1$、$F=0$，所有二阶偏导为零，$e=f=g=0$。每个 $q$ 处，若 $w=aX_u+bX_v$、$z=cX_u+dX_v$，则 $\mathrm I_X(q;w,z)=ac+bd$，$\mathrm{II}_{X,\boldsymbol N}(q;w,z)=0$。反法向下第二形式仍为零。
